title: Software Architecture Fundamentals: Modules, Dependencies & When to Split a Service
concept: Learn the architecture decisions you make every week without calling them that: modules, layers and services, coupling and cohesion, which way dependencies point, ports for payment and email, refactoring without changing behaviour, and deciding between a modular monolith and microservices with evidence.
description: A beginner course for developers who have built a small application and now wonder why every change touches five files. Every lesson starts from a situation on the CodeDev learning platform - an OrderService that grew to 900 lines and talks to the database, email and payment directly, a refactor that sent the receipt email before the payment was confirmed, an AI-generated refactor that made two modules import each other, a team that wanted microservices because the monolith felt slow - and answers it with a decision you can check: modules, layers and services, coupling and cohesion measured as fan-in and fan-out, dependency direction, ports and adapters, refactoring behind tests, the Monolith or Microservices scenario, shared databases, the signals that justify splitting a service, and architecture decision records. 10 lessons with True/False quizzes on real code and situations, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Tell modules, layers and services apart and choose the simplest structure that works
Measure coupling as fan-in and fan-out and spot modules that do too much
Keep dependencies pointing one way and find layer violations and import cycles
Put payment and email behind ports and refactor while keeping behaviour, guarded by tests
Decide between a modular monolith and microservices with evidence and record the decision in an ADR
